resistor-symbol.context: The zigzag resistor symbol with a lead on each end, as drawn on circuit diagrams. Use it for resistors, resistance values, schematic editors and electronics lessons.

potentiometer-symbol.context: A zigzag resistor with an arrow wiper pointing at its middle, the schematic symbol for a potentiometer. Use it for pots, adjustable resistors, volume controls and circuit diagrams.

capacitor-symbol.context: Two parallel plates with a lead on each side, the schematic symbol for a capacitor. Use it for capacitors, capacitance, filters and circuit diagrams.

variable-capacitor-symbol.context: Two capacitor plates with a diagonal arrow drawn through them, marking a capacitor whose value can be changed. Use it for tuning capacitors, trimmers and radio circuits.

inductor-symbol.context: A row of four coil humps with a lead on each end, the schematic symbol for an inductor. Use it for inductors, coils, chokes and circuit diagrams.

iron-core-inductor-symbol.context: Coil humps with two straight lines above them for the magnetic core, the schematic symbol for an iron core inductor or choke. Use it in power supply and audio circuit diagrams.

transformer-symbol.context: Two coils facing each other with two core lines between them, the schematic symbol for a transformer. Use it for transformers, isolation, step up and step down voltage in circuit diagrams.

diode-symbol.context: A triangle pointing at a bar on a signal line, the schematic symbol for a diode. Use it for diodes, rectifiers, one way current flow and circuit diagrams.

led-symbol.context: A diode symbol with two small arrows pointing away from it for emitted light, the schematic symbol for an LED. Use it for light emitting diodes, indicators and circuit diagrams.

schottky-diode-symbol.context: A diode triangle pointing at a bar whose ends bend into small hooks, the schematic symbol for a Schottky diode. Use it for fast, low voltage drop diodes in power and switching circuits.

tunnel-diode-symbol.context: A diode triangle pointing at a bar with flags at both ends that make a bracket, the schematic symbol for a tunnel diode. Use it in high frequency and oscillator circuit diagrams.

varactor-diode-symbol.context: A diode triangle and bar followed by a capacitor plate, the schematic symbol for a varactor. Use it for voltage controlled capacitance, tuning and radio circuit diagrams.

tvs-diode-symbol.context: Two diode triangles pointing at one bar with bent tips, the schematic symbol for a bidirectional TVS diode. Use it for surge, ESD and transient protection in circuit diagrams.

npn-transistor-symbol.context: A bipolar transistor in a circle with a base bar, collector and emitter, and an arrow pointing out on the emitter. Use it for NPN transistors, amplifiers and switches in circuit diagrams.

pnp-transistor-symbol.context: A bipolar transistor in a circle with a base bar, collector and emitter, and an arrow pointing in on the emitter. Use it for PNP transistors, high side switches and circuit diagrams.

mosfet-symbol.context: A gate plate beside a broken three part channel with drain, source and a body arrow, the schematic symbol for an enhancement MOSFET. Use it for power switching, motor drivers and circuit diagrams.

jfet-symbol.context: A channel bar with drain and source leads and a gate arrow meeting it, inside a circle: the schematic symbol for a junction field effect transistor. Use it for JFET amplifiers and circuit diagrams.

igbt-symbol.context: An insulated gate plate beside a transistor bar with collector and an emitter arrow, the schematic symbol for an IGBT. Use it for inverters, motor drives and power electronics diagrams.

thyristor-symbol.context: A diode triangle and bar with a gate lead angled off the bar, the schematic symbol for a thyristor or SCR. Use it for controlled rectifiers, power control and circuit diagrams.

triac-symbol.context: Two opposing diode triangles between two bars with a gate lead, the schematic symbol for a triac. Use it for AC switching, light dimmers, motor speed control and circuit diagrams.

diac-symbol.context: Two opposing diode triangles between two bars without a gate, the schematic symbol for a diac. Use it for triac triggering, dimmer circuits and circuit diagrams.

phototransistor-symbol.context: A transistor inside a circle with two arrows of light pointing at its base, the schematic symbol for a phototransistor. Use it for light sensors, optical detectors and circuit diagrams.

optocoupler-symbol.context: A box holding an LED and a phototransistor with light arrows between them, the schematic symbol for an optocoupler. Use it for galvanic isolation, isolated inputs and circuit diagrams.

photoresistor-symbol.context: A resistor box inside a circle with two light arrows pointing at it, the schematic symbol for a light dependent resistor. Use it for light sensing, dusk switches and circuit diagrams.

varistor-symbol.context: A resistor box crossed by a diagonal line with a short flat tail, the schematic symbol for a varistor. Use it for surge suppression, overvoltage protection and circuit diagrams.

spdt-switch-symbol.context: A lever on a pivot touching one of two contacts, the schematic symbol for a single pole double throw changeover switch. Use it for selectors, changeover contacts and circuit diagrams.

dpdt-switch-symbol.context: Two changeover switches whose levers are linked by a dashed line, the schematic symbol for a double pole double throw switch. Use it for reversing, ganged switching and circuit diagrams.

reed-switch-symbol.context: An open switch drawn inside a capsule outline, the schematic symbol for a reed switch. Use it for magnetic sensors, door contacts and circuit diagrams.

relay-coil-symbol.context: A coil box linked by a dashed line to a switch contact, the schematic symbol for a relay. Use it for relays, contactors, control circuits and wiring diagrams.

circuit-breaker-symbol.context: A switch lever lifted off its contact with a small hook arc over the gap, a schematic sign for a circuit breaker. Use it for overcurrent protection, tripped breakers and wiring diagrams.

speaker-symbol.context: A small box joined to a flared cone with two leads, the schematic symbol for a loudspeaker. Use it for audio outputs, speakers and circuit diagrams.

microphone-symbol.context: A circle with a straight bar along one side and two leads, the schematic symbol for a microphone. Use it for audio inputs, microphones and circuit diagrams.

antenna-symbol.context: A vertical lead topped by an upside down triangle, the schematic symbol for an antenna. Use it for aerials, radio inputs, RF circuits and circuit diagrams.

ammeter-symbol.context: A circle with a letter A inside and a lead on each side, the schematic symbol for an ammeter. Use it for current measurement in circuit diagrams and physics lessons.

voltmeter-symbol.context: A circle with a letter V inside and a lead on each side, the schematic symbol for a voltmeter. Use it for voltage measurement in circuit diagrams and physics lessons.

signal-ground-symbol.context: A vertical lead ending in a downward pointing triangle, the schematic symbol for signal ground. Use it for ground references, common returns and circuit diagrams.

xnor-gate.context: An OR gate shape with a doubled curved back and a bubble on its output, the logic symbol for an XNOR gate. Use it for digital logic, equality checks and circuit diagrams.

buffer-gate.context: A plain triangle pointing right with one input and one output, the logic symbol for a buffer. Use it for signal drivers, repeaters and digital circuit diagrams.

schmitt-trigger-symbol.context: A buffer triangle with a small hysteresis loop inside, the logic symbol for a Schmitt trigger. Use it for debouncing, clean switching thresholds and circuit diagrams.

tri-state-buffer-symbol.context: A buffer triangle with an enable line entering from the top, the logic symbol for a tri-state buffer. Use it for shared data buses, output enable and digital circuit diagrams.

d-flip-flop.context: A block with D and clock inputs, a clock wedge and two outputs, the logic symbol for a D flip-flop. Use it for latches, registers, sequential logic and digital design.

multiplexer-symbol.context: A trapezoid wider on the input side with several inputs, a select line and one output, the symbol for a multiplexer. Use it for data selectors, routing and digital circuit diagrams.

comparator-symbol.context: A triangle with two inputs and a step waveform inside, the symbol for a voltage comparator. Use it for threshold detection, analog to digital decisions and circuit diagrams.

adc-converter.context: A box split by a diagonal with a smooth sine wave on one side and a staircase on the other, a block for an analog to digital converter. Use it for sampling, digitizing and data acquisition.

voltage-regulator-symbol.context: A block with input and output leads, a ripple turning into a flat line inside, and a ground lead below: a voltage regulator. Use it for power supply design and circuit diagrams.

wire-junction-symbol.context: Two wires crossing with a solid dot where they meet, the schematic sign for a connected junction. Use it for nodes, wire connections and circuit diagrams.

test-point-symbol.context: A wire ending in a small open circle, the schematic sign for a test point. Use it for probe points, measurement pads and PCB test documentation.

thermocouple-symbol.context: Two wires of different weight meeting in a V at a dot, with plus and minus marks, the schematic symbol for a thermocouple. Use it for temperature sensing and instrumentation diagrams.

spark-gap-symbol.context: Two leads ending in points that face each other across a small gap, the schematic symbol for a spark gap. Use it for surge arresters, ignition and high voltage circuit diagrams.

neon-lamp-symbol.context: A circle holding two parallel electrodes and a dot for the gas, the schematic symbol for a neon lamp. Use it for glow lamps, mains indicators and circuit diagrams.

crystal-symbol.context: A small block between two parallel plates with a lead on each side, the schematic symbol for a quartz crystal. Use it for clocks, oscillators, resonators and circuit diagrams.

hall-sensor-symbol.context: A square crossed by an X with a lead on each of its four sides, a symbol for a Hall effect sensor. Use it for magnetic field sensing, current sensing and circuit diagrams.

pwm-signal.context: A pulse train whose flat topped pulses change width, the waveform of pulse width modulation. Use it for duty cycle, motor and LED dimming control, and signal settings.

signal-noise.context: A flat line broken by a jagged, random spiky trace, showing noise on a signal. Use it for interference, static, jitter and signal quality settings.

am-modulation.context: A fast carrier wave whose peaks swell and shrink with a slow envelope, showing amplitude modulation. Use it for AM radio, modulation settings and signal lessons.

fm-modulation.context: A wave of constant height whose cycles bunch up in the middle and spread out at the ends, showing frequency modulation. Use it for FM radio, modulation settings and signal lessons.

smd-resistor.context: A flat rectangular chip with metal end caps and a printed code, a surface mount resistor. Use it for SMD parts, PCB assembly, component stores and bills of materials.

resistor-network.context: A flat single row package with pins along its bottom edge and a dot at pin one, a resistor network. Use it for resistor arrays, pull up banks and component catalogues.

ceramic-disc-capacitor.context: A flat round disc on two thin bent legs, a ceramic disc capacitor. Use it for decoupling capacitors, through hole parts and component catalogues.

film-capacitor.context: A boxy block with rounded corners, a printed capacitor mark and two legs, a film capacitor. Use it for box capacitors, audio and power parts, and component catalogues.

tantalum-capacitor.context: A small teardrop bead with a plus mark and two legs, a tantalum bead capacitor. Use it for polarized capacitors, power decoupling and component catalogues.

supercapacitor.context: A wide squat coin shaped can with a large plus sign and two legs, a supercapacitor. Use it for energy storage, backup power and component catalogues.

trimmer-potentiometer.context: A small square block with a slotted round adjuster on top and three pins below, a trimmer potentiometer. Use it for trim pots, calibration and component catalogues.

slide-potentiometer.context: A long body with a lever and square knob that slides along it, and pins below: a slide potentiometer. Use it for faders, linear controls and component catalogues.

rotary-switch.context: A round knob with a pointer and a ring of position dots, a rotary switch. Use it for multi position selectors, band switches and control panels.

dip-switch.context: A small block with a row of slide toggles, some up and some down, a DIP switch. Use it for configuration settings, address selection and hardware options.

tactile-switch.context: A small square base with four legs and a round push button, a tactile switch. Use it for push buttons, reset buttons and component catalogues.

slide-switch.context: A small box with a sliding nub on top and three pins below, a slide switch. Use it for on off switches, mode selection and component catalogues.

reed-switch.context: A glass capsule with two overlapping metal reeds and a lead out of each end, a reed switch. Use it for magnetic sensors, door and window alarms and component catalogues.

tilt-switch.context: A leaning can with a metal ball resting in its lower corner and two legs, a tilt switch. Use it for tilt and orientation sensing, vibration alarms and component catalogues.

selector-switch.context: A round panel switch with a bar handle across its face and two position marks, a selector switch. Use it for control panels, mode selection and industrial controls.

panel-indicator-light.context: A domed lens on a flange and threaded body with short rays, a panel indicator light. Use it for pilot lights, status lamps and control panel design.

dip-chip.context: A rectangular chip seen from above with a notch at one end and legs along both long sides, a DIP integrated circuit. Use it for chips, through hole ICs and electronics projects.

soic-chip.context: A low, wide chip with short legs along its two long sides and a pin one dot, an SOIC surface mount package. Use it for SMD chips, PCB assembly and component catalogues.

qfp-chip.context: A square flat chip with legs along all four sides and a dot in one corner, a quad flat package. Use it for microcontrollers, SMD chips and PCB design.

bga-chip.context: A square chip seen from below with a grid of round solder balls and a cut pin one corner, a ball grid array. Use it for BGA packages, reflow soldering and PCB design.

metal-can-transistor.context: A short round metal can with a small tab on its rim and three legs below, a metal can transistor. Use it for vintage transistors, through hole parts and component catalogues.

ic-socket.context: An open rectangular frame with a row of contact holes along both long sides, an IC socket. Use it for chip sockets, through hole assembly and component catalogues.
